art.subject: Grey-sided Thrush (Turdus feae), adult male in spring: upperparts warm olive-brown from crown to tail; a white supercilium and a white crescent below the eye; dark lores; chin and throat white; breast and flanks plain grey; centre of the belly and undertail coverts white; wings and tail olive-brown; bill dark with a yellow base to the lower mandible; dark eye; pale yellowish-brown legs.
art.pose: standing on the forest floor among leaf litter, side view
art.scene: deciduous woodland floor on a Korean offshore island in May, dappled light; no people, buildings or text
art.build: A medium-sized thrush, smaller and slimmer than a Dusky Thrush and very like an Eyebrowed Thrush in size and shape, with a rounded head. Bill straight, slightly shorter than the head. Legs medium, pale. Tail medium, square, plain. Shy, feeding on the ground in forest.
avoid: Do not paint orange flanks; that is Eyebrowed Thrush (Turdus obscurus). This species has a grey breast and flanks.
Do not paint a grey head; the crown and face are olive-brown with a white supercilium.
Do not spot or streak the underparts.
